matches.rationale: No finding flags the inflated dataset size of 38,364 for FT‑HID; pred 4 reports the correct size 9,120 and discusses unit inconsistency, which does not capture the data fabrication.
No finding mentions Rodrigues’ formula, the rotation matrix error, or the sign flip in the (1−cosθ) term.
No finding identifies the missing batch size, learning rate schedule, or other training details; the corruption is not observed.
No finding challenges the abstract’s ‘first egocentric realistic world simulator’ claim or cites conflicting prior works.
No finding detects the fabricated ‘Matrix-Game [49]’ citation or questions the existence of the reference.

Although pred 1 discusses indoor vs. general Nymeria tables, it refers to Table 2 and Table 5, not the corrupted Table 3 that masks the full benchmark as indoor only. The underlying omission and biased evaluation are not captured.
Pred 7 directly examines Equation (1) and flags the unexplained βt term as non‑standard/possible error, matching the corruption that introduces an undefined β into the diffusion forward process.
No finding mentions the asymmetrical use of Qwen2.5‑VL to enrich competitor captions while PlayerOne uses motion sequences, and no baseline unfairness is highlighted.
No finding disputes the over‑generalised ‘diverse scenarios’ conclusion drawn from a limited 100‑video indoor benchmark.
No finding notes the removal of the anonymisation statement or any ethical omission regarding human subjects and consent.
No finding identifies the promotional language ‘completely solves’ or ‘eliminates all limitations’ as rhetorical inflation.

Pred 6 explicitly contrasts the abstract’s ‘true real‑time generation at 30 FPS’ with 8‑8.4 FPS in the experiments, capturing the same cross‑section inconsistency between abstract and body about real‑time capability.
No finding reports the fabricated PlayerOne MPJPE of 98.42 in the ablation Table 2 or its contradiction with Table 3’s value 127.16.
No finding flags the dimensional mismatch when zmotion is changed from 3 to 5 channels and the resulting DiT input inconsistency.
No finding points out the contradiction between the conclusion’s ‘ensures coherent world generation’ claim and the documented limitations on game scenarios.
